lines.text: There's a lot of us under one roof. Somebody's always cooking and somebody's always complaining about it.
My family's small, but loud. We argue over the last pickle every single night.
My grandparents still live with us. I hear the same three stories every week, and I'd miss them if they stopped.
That's enough of my family for one day. They'd be embarrassed I said so much.
I've told you all about the household already. Nothing's changed since lunch.
My family? That's a bit close to home, {player}. We've only just met.
I don't talk about my people with someone I barely know.
We eat together every night, all of us, even when someone's sulking. Especially then.
My parents taught me to ask why. They regret it at least once a day.
I've a little cousin who copies everything I do. So I walk backwards everywhere now, just to see.
My family has never left the Leaf. Not once in three generations. I'll be the first.
I keep the family calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, the day the roof needs checking. Nobody else would.
I look after my parents now. It's no burden. They looked after me for long enough.
There's a few of us. We get on. Quietly.
My grandmother tells stories about a fox who lives in the well. I still check the well.
Everyone in my house works. Even the youngest sorts the beans. That's how we get by.
I've been piecing together our family tree. There's a whole branch nobody will tell me about. Probably dull.
I'd do anything for my family. Anything. I check the locks twice before bed.
My little sister is learning to read. I sit with her every evening. She's so proud of every word.
My family's name is older than the street it lives on. I carry it carefully.
My family's the BEST! Loud, stubborn and the strongest grip on this side of the village!
They're kind to me. They don't push. I'm grateful for that.
My parents served. Their parents served. I serve. It's what we do.
Thank you for telling me, {player}. I won't carry it anywhere it shouldn't go.
That's a lot to hold on your own. You don't have to, you know.
I'm glad you trust me with that. Come and talk any time it gets heavy.
I'm still thinking about what you told me earlier. I'm here if there's more.
We've talked a lot today. Let it settle, {player}. I'm not going anywhere.
I'm glad you'd share, but maybe wait until you know me better.
That sounds important. Keep it a while longer, until you're sure of me.
Oh, come here. You've been carrying that all alone? Not anymore. Eat something, and keep talking.
I'll think about what you said. Carefully. It deserves that.
No jokes. Not for this. Thank you for telling me, {player}. Really.
Everyone's walking some road. Yours sounds harder than most. I'd like to walk some of it with you.
I'll remember every word. Not to hold it against you. To understand you properly.
Then I'll be someone you can count on. Whatever comes. That's a promise.
I... don't really know what to say. I'm not good with this sort of thing.
Thank you. Your story's still being written, you know. The best chapters might be the next ones.
That's hard. And you're still standing. That tells me more about you than any of it.
I've wondered about you for so long, and I'm glad I didn't have to ask. Thank you.
Nobody's going to make you feel that way again. Not while I'm around.
Thank you for trusting me. Take your time. I'll listen to all of it.
You've no reason to be ashamed of any of that. Hold your head up. I will, for you.
That's so unfair! You don't deserve any of it! I'm on your side, {player}, always!
I... I know a little what that's like. Thank you for telling me. Really.
That took courage. More than most missions. I'm proud of you for saying it.
Oh, very funny. I'll get you back for that, {player}.
Ha! Fine, I walked into that one.
You're lucky I like you.
Once was funny. Twice is pushing it.
Running out of material, are we?
We don't know each other well enough for that.
Careful. Teasing's for friends, and we're not there yet.
Cheeky! See if I save you the crispy bit of the rice now.
Hm. That was actually quite clever. I'll laugh later, when I've thought of a reply.
Oh, it's ON. You'd better sleep with one eye open, {player}.
Ha! Says the one who got lost in the bamboo by the river. Twice.
That's not accurate, but it is funny. I'll allow it.
Fair. I deserved that one. Next one's mine, though.
...Hm. Not bad.
You've just given me an idea for a very unflattering painting of you. Thank you.
Funny. Charge you a ryo for every joke at my expense and I'd be rich.
Wait, is that true? Do I really do that? I do, don't I. Oh no.
Laugh all you like. I'll still walk you home.
That's a little mean. ...A little funny, too.
I beg your pardon? Do you know who you're talking to?
WHAT?! Take that back! ...Okay, it was funny. TAKE IT BACK ANYWAY!
Oh... I didn't... is that what people think of me?
That's enough. Mockery is a poor habit, {player}.
I try to leave every place a little better than I found it. That's all.
Keep your word. If you can't keep it, don't give it.
Treat people the same whether they can do something for you or not.
I've preached enough for one day, {player}.
You know what I believe now. Let's see if I live up to it.
What I believe in? That's not something I share with just anyone.
Ask me that when you've seen how I live. Then you'll know.
Kindness and family. Feed people, look after your own, and count everyone as your own.
Know things, and tell the truth about what you know. Everything else follows.
Be free and be kind. Life's too short to be cruel or cooped up.
Courage, and freedom to use it. A wall's only there to be looked over.
Do your duty, and do it well enough that nobody has to check.
Duty and loyalty. Stand where you said you'd stand, with who you said you'd stand by.
Honesty. And being left to live my own way.
Make things. Make the world stranger and more beautiful. And let others do the same.
Tell the truth, pay your debts, do the work. Simple, not easy.
Never stop asking questions. And never let anyone tell you that you can't.
Loyalty to the people you love. Family first, and family is whoever you'd bleed for.
Be kind. Especially to the small things that can't thank you.
Strength, and the honour of my family. One protects the other.
Courage! Loyalty! Never give up on your friends, and never run away!
I think... making something gentle and true is a brave thing. And being kind is, too.
Duty. Loyalty. Discipline holds them together.
Sleep on it. Most things look smaller after breakfast.
Ask the person it concerns, not everyone around them.
When in doubt, do the kind thing and the honest thing. Usually they're the same.
I've given you all my wisdom for today. It's not a deep well, {player}.
Try the advice I gave you first, then come back.
I'm hardly the one to ask. We barely know each other.
Advice from a near stranger? Ask someone who knows you.
Eat first. Then decide. Nobody ever made a good choice hungry.
Write both choices down and read them aloud. You'll hear which one you already want.
Flip a coin. If you're disappointed with how it lands, do the other thing.
Take the road that scares you a little. Not a lot. A little.
Break it into steps. Small ones. Then do the first one today.
Keep the promise you already made. Then worry about the next one.
Say less. Watch more.
Imagine you're telling the story of it years from now. Which version would you be proud of?
What does it cost, and what's it worth? If you can't answer both, you're not ready.
Find out more first. Most bad choices are just choices made too early.
Whatever you do, don't do it alone. Take someone you trust.
Be gentle with yourself. And with whoever's on the other side of it.
Do nothing you'd be ashamed to put your name to. That's my family's rule. Use it.
Go for it! Full force! If it goes wrong, go for it again!
Um. I'd... I'd do the thing that feels a bit brave. Small brave. That's usually right.
Stop asking and start doing. You already know the answer.
I've a dream I've never said out loud. I'll say it to you. Just this once.
Some mornings I wake up and the dream feels close enough to touch. Other mornings it's over the mountains.
Everyone laughs when you're young and say what you want to be. I stopped saying it. I never stopped wanting it.
I've said enough about my dream for one day. Let me keep a little of it to myself.
You've heard it now. Hold me to it, {player}.
My dream? That's... not for someone I barely know.
You haven't earned that one yet, {player}. Not yet.
I want a home full of people, all fed and safe. That's my dream. Is it too small? It feels big to me.
I want to understand one thing completely before I die. I haven't chosen which yet.
Promise you won't laugh. ...You can laugh a little. I mean it, though. Every word.
I want to stand somewhere nobody from the Leaf has ever stood. Then come home and tell you about it.
I have a plan for my dream. Forty steps. I'm on step nine.
It's not a flashy dream. But I'll get there a day at a time. I always do.
I've never told anyone. ...Don't make me regret it.
When I close my eyes I can see it already, every colour. I just have to make the world catch up.
A dream's just a plan nobody's paid for yet. I'm saving up.
I keep wondering whether my dream will look the way I picture it when I get there. Do you think it will?
My dream's about the people I love. Keeping them safe is part of it. All of it, maybe.
It's a quiet dream. I hope that's all right. I think quiet dreams count too.
My dream is worthy of my name. I'll reach it, or I'll fall trying. There's no third choice.
I'm going to do it! I'm going to do it if it takes a hundred years! You'll see!
I've only ever written it in my diary. Saying it out loud is... scary. Here goes.
A dream without discipline is a wish. Mine has a schedule.
I worry about the people I love more than I let them see.
I worry I'm running out of time to become who I meant to be.
Some nights I lie awake wondering if I've chosen the wrong road.
I've said my worries out loud once today. That's enough to get me to sleep.
Thank you for listening earlier. Let's talk about something lighter.
My worries are my own, {player}.
Let's not dig into that. Not with someone I've only just got to know.
I worry I'm not doing enough for everyone. There's always someone hungry I didn't notice.
I worry that I think so much I never actually act. Then the moment's gone.
I worry people think I'm only a joke. That I'll never be taken seriously when it matters.
What if I never leave? What if I'm old in this same street, wondering what was out there?
I'm afraid of the mistake I didn't catch. The one that hurts somebody.
I worry about letting someone down. Once. When it matters. That's the one I couldn't live with.
That I'll keep everyone at arm's length until there's no one left to reach.
I worry the colours will fade. That one day I'll look at the sky and just see sky.
Money. Always money. One bad season and everything I've built is gone.
I worry there's an answer I'll never find. It keeps me up, honestly.
That I won't be there when someone needs me. That I'll be a step too slow.
I worry the world is too hard for soft things. And I'm one of them.
I worry I'll shame my family. That I'm not as strong as they believe.
I worry I'll give it everything and it still won't be enough. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.
That I'll never be brave enough to say the things I really mean.
That I've been too hard on the people I'm trying to make strong. That they'll only remember the hardness.
We've had some good times already, haven't we? I keep a few of them close.
I was just remembering the last time we went out. That was a good day.
I've been through all our good memories once today. Let's make a new one.
We've reminisced enough, {player}. Let's go and do something worth remembering.
We haven't got many memories yet, you and I. Give it time.
Ask me again after we've been out together a few times.
Nothing new since we last talked. Quiet weeks are underrated.
Still waiting to see how things land. I'll tell you as soon as I know.
I've no news beyond what I told you earlier.
Same as this morning, {player}. Nothing's moved.
Nothing to tell yet. Ask me in a week or two.
It's too early to say how it's going.
Not much to report. The well bucket squeaks again, and nobody's oiled it.
Busy morning, slow afternoon. The usual.
Did you see the sky at dawn? Pink all the way to the Hokage Rock.
Let's leave that for when we know each other better.
That's a conversation for another day, I think.
Ask me again in a while, {player}. Not yet.
Them? One of the best people I know. I'd do anything for them.
I'd walk through the rain to bring them soup. That's how I feel about them.
Don't you say a word against them. They're dear to me.
I like them. Good company, always on time.
They're all right. More than all right, honestly.
We get on well. They make me laugh.
I don't really know them. We nod in the street.
Them? Can't say I've an opinion. Seem decent enough.
We've spoken once or twice. Nothing to tell.
We're not close. Let's leave it at that.
They and I don't see eye to eye. It's nothing dramatic.
I keep my distance. It's better for both of us.
I'd rather not talk about them. Or to them.
Honestly? I can't stand them. Don't tell anyone I said it.
If they're coming, I'm leaving. That's all I'll say.
We've done the weather already, {player}. The sky hasn't changed its mind.
Still the same day, still the same squeaky bucket.
Let's start simpler, shall we?
We hardly know each other. Hello is plenty for now.
Grilled mackerel with a squeeze of citrus. Nothing fancier needed.
Have you tried the eel by the second bridge? They brush it with sauce three times.
I'd eat dango every day if my teeth would let me.
We've talked food already today. Now I'm just hungry.
If we keep talking about food, I'll have to go and buy some.
Food? We've only just met. Ask me when we've shared a meal.
Let's get to know each other a little first.
Miso soup, the way my grandmother made it. I'll make you a bowl. No, I insist.
I like plain rice and pickles. You can taste every grain when nothing's shouting over it.
I can fit six dango in my mouth at once. I'll show you. Okay, five. Okay, maybe don't watch.
A merchant once gave me a pepper from the far south. I cried for an hour. I'd do it again.
Rolled omelette, cut into exactly eight. Uneven pieces taste wrong. I can't explain it.
Rice, fish, soup. Same breakfast for twelve years. It's never let me down.
Cold soba. Quiet place. That's it.
Sweet bean buns taste like a lazy afternoon. Do you know what I mean? Purple and slow.
Whatever's freshest and cheapest at the stalls. The fishmonger marks down at four, by the way.
How do they get the broth at Ichiraku so clear? I've asked. They just wink.
You're eating properly, aren't you? Not just ramen? ...Mostly ramen. I knew it.
I like warm sweet potato in winter. I share the skins with the neighbour's dog.
My family's pickling recipe goes back five generations. Nothing in the market compares.
RAMEN! Extra pork! Extra egg! Extra everything! Is there any other answer?
I like... strawberry mochi. Is that silly? It's soft. It doesn't make a fuss.
Food is fuel. Brown rice, grilled fish, and no sweets before a mission.
I'm working on my footwork. Slow, but it's coming.
Training Ground 3 has the best posts. The bark's worn to the shape of a fist.
Every morning, a lap of the outer wall. Some mornings I even enjoy it.
We've already compared bruises today, {player}.
More training talk? Go and actually train, then come back.
I don't talk technique with people I've just met.
Let's leave training for when we've sparred once or twice.
I mostly train so I can carry the shopping up the hill without stopping. It counts!
Most mistakes in a spar happen in the head first. I train my thinking as much as my arms.
I train by racing the pigeons off the roofs. They win. For now.
I climb the cliff behind the falls. No ropes. Don't tell anyone. Want to come?
Three hundred strikes, logged. Then I check where the misses went and adjust.
Same drills every day. They're dull. That's why they work.
I train alone. Early. Before anyone's watching.
I pretend the training post is a mountain troll. It helps more than you'd think.
Train what you'll use. Fancy jutsu won't help if you can't run for an hour.
Why does a spinning kunai fly straighter? I threw two hundred to find out. Still not sure.
I practise guarding more than striking. Someone has to stand in front.
Oh... I don't really like fighting talk. Could we talk about something else?
I train harder than anyone my age. That's not a boast. Ask the posts.
A thousand kicks before breakfast! Then a thousand more! Want to join? You want to!
I practise throwing at night, when nobody can see me miss. I'm getting better. A little.
Train until the movement is boring. Then train it until it's yours.
Oh, go on. ...No, really, go on, say it again.
That's kind of you, {player}. You made my morning.
You noticed? Nobody notices. Thank you.
Twice in one day? You'll turn my head, {player}.
Careful, you'll use up all your nice words on me.
That's... a bit much from someone I barely know. But thank you.
Flattery already? We've only just met.
Aren't you sweet! Here, have a rice cake for that.
Thank you. I'll think about that, actually. It's nice to be seen.
I KNOW. But it's nice to hear. Say it in a funny voice this time.
Ha! Thanks. Tell that to the mountain that nearly threw me off last week.
You noticed the stitching? Six hours. Thank you. Truly.
Thank you, {player}. That means more from you than most.
...Don't. I don't know what to do with that.
That's the nicest thing I've heard all week. I'm going to paint it. Somehow.
Kind words don't pay the rent. But fine. Thank you. Now, was there something you needed?
Really? What makes you say that? No, I want to know, tell me exactly.
Thank you. Now you look after yourself as well as you say I do.
Oh. That's lovely of you. I'll keep that one somewhere safe.
Naturally. ...But I'm glad it was you who said it.
YES! Thank you! Now I'm fired up for the whole day!
M-me? Oh. Thank you. I don't... thank you.
Hm. Praise is easy. But I'll accept it. Once.
The tea house is putting in a second bench by the river. Big news, for our street.
They're repainting the gate posts. Somebody chose a very loud red.
The bathhouse raised its prices by a ryo. People are furious. Quietly.
That's all the news I've got. I'm not making any up.
You've heard the lot, {player}. Come back tomorrow for fresh gossip.
I don't pass gossip to people I've only just met.
News? Maybe once I know where it'll end up.
The baker's daughter is walking now! Wobbly as a new foal. The whole lane cheered.
The Academy library had a flood in the cellar. They're drying the scrolls on the roof, page by page.
Somebody painted a moustache on the scarecrow by the farms. It wasn't me. It was definitely not me.
A caravan came in from the far east this morning. Silk, spices and a goat with a hat.
The Mission Desk changed its filing order. Nobody can find anything. I've offered to help.
The night watch doubled on the east wall for the season. Nothing wrong, just careful.
I don't keep up with gossip. Ask someone else.
The wisteria by the shrine bloomed overnight. People say it does that when a baby's born on the street.
Rice is up two ryo a sack. Buy now if you can, it'll be worse after the rains.
Did you hear? Someone found a tunnel under the old storehouse. Just a root cellar, probably. Probably!
There's a loose dog near the market biting at ankles. Mind the little ones if you see it.
The kennel had a litter of pups. Seven! They're looking for homes.
Our clan's youngest passed the Academy entrance with the top mark. As expected.
There's going to be a sumo match at the stadium! I'm entering! Probably! Maybe!
The flower shop has a new colour of iris. Sort of a grey-blue. I went to look three times.
Two Genin were caught on the Hokage Rock after curfew. Laps till dawn. Rightly so.
I whittle little animals in the evenings. I've a shelf of crooked foxes.
I keep a garden box on the sill. Two radishes this year. Champion radishes.
I collect river stones. Smooth ones. My shelves are getting heavy.
I've bored you with my hobby enough for one day.
That's my hobby, the whole of it. There's no more to tell today.
What I do with my evenings is my own business. For now.
That's a bit personal for someone I've just met.
I knit. Scarves, hats, little covers for teapots. Everyone on the lane has one whether they want it or not.
I read. Histories mostly. I keep notes in the margins, which the librarian forgives me for.
I make up games. My latest is roof tag, where the ground is lava. Rules are still evolving.
I draw maps. Every path in the woods I've walked. There's a lot of blank paper left.
I keep a bonsai. Eleven years. I trim it with tweezers on the first of every month.
I carve handles for tools. A good handle lasts longer than the blade. I like that.
Calligraphy. Alone. One word, a hundred times, until it's right.
I paint. Mostly the sky, but sometimes the sky as it ought to be. More purple.
I fix broken things and sell them on. Profitable, and it keeps the hands busy.
I take clocks apart. Putting them back together is the part I'm still learning.
I teach the little ones on my street to fall without hurting themselves. Somebody should.
I look after the stray cats by the shrine. They have names. They don't answer to them.
I study my family's records. Every name, every deed. I'll add my own one day.
Training IS my hobby! And eating after training! And then more training!
I fold paper cranes. I'm at four hundred and twelve. I'm not counting for any reason. Well...
I keep my blades. Sharpen, oil, wrap. Every night. A habit of discipline.
Who, the new family by the well? Pleasant enough. They keep chickens.
I try not to say much about people who aren't here to answer.
Everyone's got a story, {player}. I only know the cover of most of them.
We've done enough talking about other people today. Let's give them a rest.
I've said all I'll say about them for now.
Gossip about the neighbours? Not with a near stranger, {player}.
Let's not start on other folk just yet.
Oh, I know everyone! Well, I know something about everyone. Who are we talking about?
I don't discuss people behind their backs. Neither should you.
I only know good things about my neighbours. I make sure of it, I feed them all.
I mind my own. They mind theirs.
I could tell you who snores loudest on this street. But then I'd have to admit how I know.
Rice balls with salted plum inside. The sour makes my whole face scrunch up, and I love it.
Hot roasted sweet potato from the cart by the gate. The paper bag's half the fun.
Anything grilled on a stick. If it's on a stick, I'll try it.
I could live on the miso ramen at Ichiraku. I might already be.
Tamagoyaki, sweet, not salty. People fight about this. I'm right.
Chestnuts in autumn. Burnt fingers every year and I never learn.
Shaved ice with strawberry syrup. Summer isn't summer without it.
Cold noodles on a hot day, with a lot of spring onion.
Fresh tofu from the tofu maker by the canal. It's still warm in the morning.
Taiyaki, filled right to the tail. The cheap stall skimps on the tail.
Mochi at New Year. Toasted until it puffs up and cracks.
Grilled corn with soy sauce at the festival. I always get it on my chin.
A good bowl of miso soup after a long shift. Simple as that.
Pickles. My own. Three years in the cellar and they're finally right.
Grilled eel with a cup of warm tea, by the river, when the work's done.
Whatever my neighbour brings over in the evening. I never ask, I just eat.
Salted salmon on rice. It's what I ate before every mission, and it's never failed me.
Hot pot. One big pot, everyone's chopsticks in it, nobody leaves hungry. That's food.
I like food with a story. The baker's chestnut bread was a wedding gift once, did you know?
I invented a dango with a pickle in the middle. Nobody likes it. I like it out of spite.
I want to taste the sea. Not fish. The actual sea. People say it's salty. I want to check.
Rice should be washed three times, soaked for half an hour, and never, ever stirred.
Whatever's on the table, I'm grateful for it. Somebody worked to put it there.
Plain rice. Quietly.
If I could eat a colour, I'd eat the pink of a sunset. It'd taste like peaches, I think.
Rice keeps, beans keep, dried fish keeps. Anything that keeps is good food.
Why does bread rise? Why doesn't rice? I asked the baker and got flour on my nose.
Never eat the mushrooms in the forest unless someone who knows checks them. Promise me.
I share my lunch with the birds by the canal. They like the crusts best.
I only eat at places worth eating at. Ichiraku passes. Barely.
I once ate seven bowls of ramen in a row! The eighth beat me! I'll be back for it!
I like eating somewhere quiet. The bench by the willow. You could come, if you... if you want.
Eat slowly. Chew properly. Your body is a tool. Look after it.
I like the green dango best. The pink one tastes like the pink one's trying too hard.
I traded my rice ball for a sweet bun at lunch. Best trade ever.
My mum puts a little face on my rice with seaweed. Don't tell anyone.
I ate a whole bag of roasted chestnuts and now my tummy hurts. Worth it.
Have you tried the candy apples at the festival? You have to eat them fast or they get sticky.
I don't like fish eyes. They look at you.
I'm learning to throw with my weaker hand. It's humbling. Very humbling.
I run the stairs up the Hokage Rock. All of them. Then I lie at the top for a while.
Tree climbing without hands is harder than they make it look.
I've been working on my balance on the fence posts by the river. I fall in a lot.
Chakra control's my weak point. I can't keep a leaf on my forehead for more than a minute.
My hand signs are getting faster. Still not fast enough to show off.
I practise my throws at the old stump behind the Academy. It's full of holes now.
Footwork, footwork, footwork. My teacher won't let me learn anything else till it's right.
I did a hundred sit-ups this morning. Ninety of them were good ones.
I've started training at dawn. The training grounds are empty and the air's cold.
Water walking. I'm wet up to my knees most days.
I train before my shift. If I leave it till after, I never do it.
My knees aren't what they were. I train smarter now, not harder.
I've been drilling the new Genin on the posts. They remind me how bad I used to be.
I keep up the old drills from my Academy days. Muscle remembers what the head forgets.
I train with my little cousin. I let them win sometimes. They know, but they like it anyway.
I read about a technique before I try it. Twice. Then I try it and it goes wrong anyway.
I turned kunai practice into a game. Hit the target, get a sweet. I'm getting very good. And full.
I train in the woods, not the grounds. Roots and rocks don't stand still like posts do.
I keep a training diary. Date, drill, count, weather. You'd be amazed what it shows.
Every day. Rain or snow. Missing one day makes missing the next one easy.
Practise. Don't talk about practising.
I train to music in my head. Kicks on the drumbeat. My teacher says it shows, in a good way.
Train what keeps you alive first. Running, hiding, climbing. Then the flashy things.
Did you know your feet stick better to bark than to stone when you mould chakra? I tested it.
I practise catching people when they fall. Someone always falls.
I train because I should. I just... don't like to talk about hitting things. Sorry.
I set my targets further back than anyone else. If I'm going to miss, I'll miss something hard.
I ran ten laps of the village yesterday! I'm doing eleven today! Then twelve! Forever!
I found a corner of Training Ground 3 behind the trees. Nobody goes there. It's my spot.
Basics. Every single day. Those who skip them are the ones who get hurt.
I can hit the target from five steps now! Last week it was three.
I practised the clone sign until my fingers got stuck. Do you think fingers can get stuck forever?
Our teacher made us run around the Academy ten times. I only stopped twice.
I'm going to be the fastest thrower in our class. Just watch.
I tried to climb a tree with chakra and fell on my bottom. Everyone saw.
We had a sparring lesson today. I didn't win, but I didn't cry either.
Really? Nobody's said that to me before. I'm going to remember it.
You're just saying that. ...You're not just saying that? Oh.
That's the nicest thing I've heard all week, {player}.
Stop, you'll make me go red. Too late, isn't it?
Thank you. I needed that more than you know.
I'll be smiling about that all afternoon. Thank you.
You noticed? I spent ages on that.
That's kind. I'll try to deserve it.
Ha! I'll take it. I'll take it twice.
Oh, you. Thank you, {player}.
At my age, a compliment's worth more than ryo. Thank you, {player}.
Nobody's told me that since my Academy days. You've made my week.
That's kind of you to say. I don't hear it much behind the counter.
Well, now I'll be smiling at customers all day. They'll wonder what's wrong with me.
I'll tell my family you said so. They'll think I made it up.
Oh, that's lovely! Come here, let me give you a squeeze for that.
That's a generous thing to notice. Most people don't look closely enough.
Flattery! I love it! Do more! Do my hair next!
Thanks! Say it again on top of the Hokage Rock, so the whole village hears.
Thank you. I did redo it four times. I'm glad it showed.
Kind of you. I'll keep at it, then.
Hm. ...Let's talk about something else.
That made my insides go all golden. Is that strange? It's a good gold.

That's kind. You're the one who deserves the compliments, though.
You're very sweet. I'll keep that one close.
Of course. ...Thank you. That came out wrong. Thank you.
You think so?! You really think so?! I'm going to do even better now!
Oh. I... um. Thank you. You don't have to say that. But thank you.
Noted. Don't let it make you lazy with your own work.

Hehe. You're nice too. Not as nice as me, but nice.

Someone left a basket of persimmons at the shrine gate. Nobody knows who.

A courier came back from the far mountains with snow still on their pack. In summer!

The gate guards changed shifts. New faces at the gate this week. Be polite, they're learning.
News. Hm. I wouldn't know.
The fog came down so thick on the river this morning, the boats looked like they were floating in cloud.
The miller's raising prices next week. Flour now, cheaper than later. You heard it here.
Did you know somebody's been leaving little paper boats in the canal every morning? Who? Why? I must know.
The wall by the old storehouse is crumbling. I've told the children not to climb it. Tell them too.
A family of ducks has moved into the shrine pond. There are six ducklings. Six!
My family's colours are hung at the festival square this year. Front row. As is proper.
There's going to be a race round the whole village at the festival! I'm going to WIN it!
The bookbinder got a new shipment of blank notebooks. With cloth covers. I... looked at them for a long time.
Curfew's being enforced on the rooftops again. Good. There've been too many twisted ankles.
Guess what? There's a new kid in our class who can whistle with two fingers!
Somebody drew a frog on the blackboard and our teacher didn't notice all morning!
The big tree by the Academy has a bird nest with three eggs in it. We're not allowed to touch.
The sweet shop's giving away broken biscuits at closing time. Free!
I heard there's going to be snow next week. I'm going to build the biggest snowman.
The kennel puppies got out and ran through the market. One stole a sausage!
I collect feathers. I've got one from a hawk. Well, I think it's a hawk.
I fold paper into animals. My frogs can jump. My cranes can't fly.
I keep a little notebook of every bird I've seen in the village. Forty-two so far.
I've been learning the flute. Badly. The dogs on my street howl along.
I press flowers between the pages of old books. The library doesn't know.
I build little boats from bark and race them in the canal.
I've started drawing maps of the village from the rooftops. The streets look different from up there.
I juggle. Three balls, sometimes four. Never eggs. Not since the last time.
I spin tops. I've got one that hums when it spins. It's my favourite.
I watch the clouds and name them. That one's called Lumpy.
I sketch the people at the tea house when they're not looking. Don't tell them.
I brew my own tea from the herbs on my sill. Some of it's even drinkable.
I play go with the old men by the river on my days off. They let me lose gracefully.
I restore old furniture. There's a chest in my room that was a pile of sticks a year ago.
I keep bees on the roof. My neighbours are nervous. My honey is excellent.
I bake little cakes and leave them on doorsteps. Nobody knows it's me. Well, now you do.
I copy old poems out by hand. It's slow. That's the point. You notice every word.
I hide little painted stones around the village for people to find. I've hidden a hundred.
I collect a stone from every place I go. My shelf's mostly from the village so far. Mostly.
I sort and label seeds. Every packet in my drawer is dated and named. All two hundred.
I tend the little shrine at the end of our lane. Fresh water every morning. Nobody asked me to.
Fishing. Alone. Early.
I make up stories about the people in the market. The tofu seller is secretly a dragon, in mine.
I grow vegetables. You can't eat a hobby, unless it's a garden.
I collect questions. I write down every one nobody can answer. The book's getting fat.
I walk the lanes at dusk and check the lamps are lit. Someone has to.
I feed the koi at the shrine pond. They know me now. They swim over when I come.
Calligraphy, in my family's style. My strokes are almost as good as my grandmother's.
I collect bruises! Kidding! I collect training scrolls. And also bruises.
I write little poems. Short ones. Nobody's read them. ...Maybe you could. One day.
Gardening. Orderly rows. Weeds removed daily. It is very calming.
I collect beetles. I have a stag beetle called Mister Pinch.
I'm building a secret den in the bushes behind my house. You can see it if you swear not to tell.
I draw ninjas. Mine all have really long scarves because scarves are cool.
I'm trying to teach my cat to sit. It doesn't want to.
I collect the paper wrappers from sweets. I've got every colour except purple.
I play marbles with my cousins. I've won eleven off them. They're mad about it.
Everyone in this street has a nickname. Nobody knows their own. It's better that way.
The tofu maker's the kindest person I know. Never says a word about it.
There's a family by the canal that sings while they work. You can hear them from the bridge.
The old priest at the shrine remembers everyone's name. Even babies'.
People are mostly good, {player}. Mostly. Keep your eyes open for the rest.
I don't really know anyone well enough to say much. I'm working on it.
The children down the lane are a menace. A sweet, loud menace.
The night watch on our street waves at me every evening. I've never seen them in daylight.
There's a lantern maker who talks to every lantern before it's sold. Like saying goodbye.
My neighbours are good people. Noisy, but good. You can't have everything.
The man who runs the bathhouse has worked there since he was eight. He's seen everyone in the village with their hair wet.
The Mission Desk clerks don't get enough thanks. They hand out danger with a smile all day.
Everybody on this lane is family, as far as I'm concerned. Even the grumpy ones. Especially them.
I try to judge people by what they do when nobody's watching. It's hard to see, which is the point.
I've given everyone on the street a secret name. You're "the one with the good laugh."
The couriers are the interesting ones. They've seen roads we've only heard of.
I know everyone's routine on this street to the minute. It's not nosy. It's observant.
I'll say this about anyone: if they keep their word, I'll keep mine to them.
People talk too much about people.
Everyone's a story I only know the middle of. I fill in the beginnings myself.
Watch how someone pays their debts. It tells you everything.
Have you noticed the potter never goes out on rainy days? I've been wondering why for a month.
I keep an eye on the little ones in our lane. Their parents work late. Someone should.
Everyone's trying their best, I think. Even when it doesn't look like it.
Few people in this village meet my standards. I'll admit the blacksmith does.
Everybody in this village is amazing! Even the annoying ones! Especially them!
I don't know many people well. The ones I do know are... nice. You're nice.
I said I don't gossip. That includes about the people you think are safe to discuss.
The big kids at the Academy think they're so cool. They're not. Well, a bit.
The sweet shop lady always gives me an extra one when nobody's looking.
My best friend can burp the alphabet. Almost the whole thing.
Our teacher has eyes in the back of their head. I'm sure of it.
The old fishmonger tells the scariest stories. About eels.
There's a kid on my street who never talks. I think they're just shy. I'm going to say hi.
We have a rule at home: whoever gets back last makes the tea. I'm always last.
There's a crack in our kitchen wall where everyone's height is marked. I'm catching up.
My family's always late to everything. We call it being on family time.
We've got an old dog who thinks it's the head of the house. It might be right.
Every New Year we all squeeze into one room and tell the year's worst story. Mine usually wins.
My grandmother's the boss of our house. Nobody voted. It just happened.
We don't have much, but there's always enough for one more at the table.
My cousins live next door. The fence between our houses has a gap we all pretend isn't there.
We're not a loud family. We talk with looks mostly. You'd understand if you met us.
Somebody in my house snores like a saw. Nobody will admit who.
Our house smells of woodsmoke and miso. I'd know it anywhere.
My parents are getting older. I visit every evening now, even if it's only for a cup of tea.
I've been the one holding the house together since I was young. I don't mind. Most days.
My spouse puts up with me. That's the best thing I can say about a marriage, and I mean it kindly.
The children are growing faster than I can sew new sleeves.
Every birthday in our family, everyone cooks one dish. The table bends in the middle.
My grandfather kept a diary every day of his life. We read a page aloud on his birthday.
My family plays a prank war that's been going on for six years. I'm currently losing.
I've an aunt who travels with the merchant caravans. She brings back the best stories.
I sorted our family's shoes by size at the door. Nobody's thanked me. I'll keep doing it.
My family's always there when it matters. Same as I try to be.
We're close. We don't say it.
My little brother thinks our house is a castle. I've started drawing him the towers.
My family keeps a jar for rainy days. When it rained hard one year, the jar saved us.
My uncle won't tell anyone how he lost his eyebrow. I'll find out. One day.
I walk my little cousins to the Academy every morning. They pretend they don't need me to.
My grandmother taught me the names of all the flowers by the shrine. I teach them to the little ones now.
Our family crest is stitched inside every one of our jackets. I touch it before anything difficult.
My family arm-wrestles to decide who does the dishes! I've never lost! Well, once!
My big sister always speaks up for me. I'm trying to learn how to do it myself.
My mother never praised me. Then I found every report card I ever had, kept in a box. She kept all of them.
My little sister copies everything I do. It's annoying. And a bit nice.
My dad snores so loud the cat leaves the room.
We've got a new baby at home and nobody sleeps. Not even the baby.
My grandpa can do a magic trick with a coin. He won't tell me how.
My mum makes me wear a scarf even when it's not cold. Every day.
I've got three big brothers. I always get the smallest piece of everything.
Thank you for telling me that. I'll think about it a lot, I think.
You can tell me anything, {player}. I mean it. Anything at all.
That's not a small thing to say out loud. I'm glad you said it to me.
I didn't know. I'm sorry. I'm here, all right?
You're braver than you let on. Did you know that?
I'll keep that safe. You've got my word.
Thank you. I understand you a little better now.
You don't have to be fine all the time. Not with me.
That explains a lot. In a good way. You make more sense to me now.
Come and find me whenever you want to talk about it. Even at night.
I'm really glad you told me. I was hoping you would.
I've lived long enough to know some things don't get lighter. They get easier to carry, with company.
I'm older than you, {player}, and I still don't know what to say. Except that I'm listening.
You've done a lot of growing up on your own. You don't have to do the rest of it alone.
If anyone gives you trouble over any of that, you send them to me.
Oh, my dear friend. Come and sit by me. You don't have to finish if you don't want to.
Can I ask one question about it? Just one. Then I'll only listen.
I'm not going to joke. I'm going to sit here and be quiet for once. You can tell people I managed it.
You've come a long way, even if you never left the village. That counts as a journey.

...I'm not the right person for this. I'm sorry. I just don't know how.
If I painted what you just told me, it would be dark at the edges and bright in the middle. The middle's you.

I won't ask any more questions. That's how much this matters. Thank you.
Whatever happened, it's behind you now, and I'm beside you. That's the order of things.

That's part of who you are, and who you are is someone I respect. Don't forget it.
I'm so glad you're you, {player}! Everything you went through, and you're still you!

Pinky promise I'll keep it secret. Pinky promises can't be broken.

How dare you. ...How dare you be right.
Fine. Fine! I'm writing that one down for revenge.
Rude. Accurate, but rude.
You've been saving that one up, haven't you?

Cheek, from someone half my age. I'll allow it. This once.

Ooh, you little rascal! Come here so I can pinch your cheeks for that.

Oh, that's a declaration of war. I accept. Watch your sandals, {player}.
Big words! Say them again halfway up a cliff, and we'll see who's laughing.

Ha. Yes, I'm predictable. You always know where to find me. There are worse things.
...Hm. Funny.

Funny. Now tease me while you carry these boxes. Two birds, one stone.
Do I really ask that many questions? Do I? ...Wait. Oh no.
Tease all you like. I'll still pick you up when you trip.
Oh, you. That's not very kind. ...It is very funny though.
I don't find that amusing. Perhaps you'll find something else to say.
Oh, you want to go?! Rematch! Words or fists, you pick!
I... I know. You don't have to say it. Everyone already does.
Is that the sort of thing you say to people who are trying to help you?
Hey! That's not true! ...Okay, it's a bit true.
You're the one with mud on your face, actually. Ha!
I'm telling! ...No I'm not. But I could.
Take it back or I'll tickle you. I mean it!
That's so mean! Do another one.

Say sorry when you're wrong. Even when it's embarrassing. Especially then.
Share what you have. Even if it's only half a rice ball.
Never laugh at someone for trying.
Help when you can. Ask for help when you can't.
Be the same person on your own as you are in a crowd.
Look after the small things, and the big things look after themselves.
If someone's alone, go and stand next to them. You don't even have to talk.
A promise is a promise. Even a small one.
Be brave when it's quiet, not just when people are watching.
Always thank the cook.
Pay what you owe and owe as little as you can. My father taught me that. It's served me well.
Work hard, rest properly, and don't confuse the two.
Raise children who can say no to you. That's the hardest one.
Never take a job you'd be ashamed to explain to your neighbours.
Leave the village better for the ones who come after. That's all any of us can do.
Nobody should go to bed hungry, or sad, or alone. If I can stop one of those, I will.
If I don't know something, I say so. Pretending is how mistakes grow.
Don't let anyone make you smaller to fit their box. And be nice to everyone anyway.
Go and see for yourself. Don't let someone else tell you what's over the hill.
Finish what you start. Half-done work is worse than no work. It misleads people.
If I said I'd be there, I'm there. Rain, snow, whatever. That's who I am.
Mind your own business. Tell the truth when it's asked.
Everyone should make something, once, just because they wanted it to exist.
Say what you mean. Do what you said. Saves everyone a lot of time.
Never believe something just because everybody says it. Ask why. Then ask again.
You stand by your own. If one of us is in trouble, we're all in trouble.
Be soft with people. You never know what they're carrying.
Never shame your name. And never let anyone shame your family's while you stand there.
Never give up! And if your friend's in trouble, you RUN to them! No thinking! Just running!
I think... being gentle with people is a kind of strength. Even if it's a quiet one.
Do your duty even when nobody thanks you. Especially then. That's when it counts.
You should always share your sweets. Except the green ones. Those are mine.
It's not fair to leave someone out of a game. That's the worst thing.
If you break something, you say so. Even if you'll get in trouble. My mum says.
You stick up for your friends. Even against big kids.
Never pull a cat's tail. Or a dog's. Or anyone's.
If you make a promise you have to keep it, or your nose falls off. Probably.
Talk to the person, not about the person. It's scarier and it works better.
Do the hard thing first. The rest of the day gets easier.
If you're scared of it, that might mean it matters.
Wait until you're calm. Angry words are hard to take back.
Ask someone who's done it before. They'll know the bit nobody tells you.
Don't decide when you're hungry, tired or cross. Fix those first.
Say sorry first. It costs less than you think.
Try it for a week. If it's still wrong after a week, change it.
Be honest, but be kind about how. Both matter.
If you can't fix it today, write it down and sleep. Tomorrow you'll see it better.
Never lend what you can't afford to lose. Not ryo, not trust.
In my experience, the sensible choice and the brave choice are the same more often than you'd think.
When I was your age I worried about everything. Most of it never happened. Worry about the rest.
Don't let anyone hurry you into a promise. A good one keeps.
If you have to ask whether it's wrong, it probably is.
Bring them something warm to eat and say what you need to say. Food makes everything gentler.
Ask yourself what you'll think of this a year from now. That's usually the answer.
Make it a game. Hard things are easier when you're trying to win.
When you can't decide between two paths, take the one with the better view.
Make a list. Then cross out everything you can't change. What's left is what to do.
Show up. Whatever it is, show up for it. That's half of everything.
Don't tell everyone your plans. Just do them.
Picture the best way it could go. Then take one small step toward that picture.
Start with what you've got, not what you wish you had.
Ask a lot of questions. People like being asked, and you'll learn the bit you were missing.
Tell someone where you're going before you go. Always. That's my whole advice.
Listen first. People often tell you what they need if you're quiet long enough.
Never beg. Ask once, clearly, and stand straight while you do it.
Shout it! Whatever it is! If you mean it, say it loud and see what happens!
I'd... write it down first. Then say it. That's how I do it, anyway.
You're overthinking. Decide, act, then learn from the result.
If someone's mean to you, tell a teacher. Or a big kid. A nice big kid.
When I'm scared I count to ten. Sometimes twenty.
Just say sorry. Then it's over and you can play again.
Eat a sweet first. Everything's easier after a sweet.
If you don't know the answer, guess. Sometimes you're right!
Ask your mum. Mums know everything. Well, mine does.
I want to be the best at something. Really the best. I've nearly picked what.
I want people to remember my name. For something good.
My dream's so big I'm a bit scared of it. That's how I know it's the right one.
I think about my dream every night before I sleep. It's the last thing in my head.
I want to do something nobody in my family has ever done.
I've drawn my dream a hundred times. In every drawing I'm smiling.
When I reach it, I want you to be there. That's part of the dream now.
I've told my dream to the river, the moon and now you. You're the first who answered.
Some days the dream feels silly. Then I see someone living theirs, and it doesn't.
I don't need everyone to understand my dream. Just one or two people. You, maybe.
I had a dream when I was young. I put it down for a while. I've picked it back up.
People think it's too late for me. I don't. I've been saving for it for ten years.
My dream changed when I had a family. It got bigger, not smaller.
I want to leave something behind that lasts longer than me. That's all.
I dream about a long table with every friend I've ever had around it. All at once. Imagine!
I'd like to write something one day that makes someone think differently. Just one someone.
Promise you won't tell anyone? Okay. ...I'm still not telling. But I promise it's a good one.
There's a map in the library with a blank space in the corner. I want to be the one who fills it in.
I'll know I've reached my dream when there's nothing left on the list. I check it every night.
My dream's slow. I'm slow. We'll get there together, me and the dream.
It's mine. That's enough for now.
I dreamt my dream once, while I was asleep. It looked exactly like I hoped. I woke up crying, the happy kind.
Dreams need ryo, time and stubbornness. I've got the last one. Working on the first two.
My dream keeps changing as I learn more. Is that allowed? I think that's allowed.
If my dream comes true, nobody I love will ever have to be scared again. That's the size of it.
I hope my dream makes someone's day a little softer. That would be enough.
I'll reach it. Then I'll set a higher one. My family doesn't stop at one.
Every morning I shout my dream at the sunrise! The neighbours have complained! I don't care!
I wrote my dream on a lantern once and let it float away. Maybe it'll find its way.
I'll reach it, or I'll have trained the next one who does. Either way, it's done.
When I grow up I'm going to be a Jonin. With a cool vest and everything.
I want to have a shop that only sells sweets. Every kind. Even the weird ones.
I'm going to be the Hokage! Or the Hokage's best friend. That's almost as good.
I want to have a hundred dogs. Maybe fifty. Okay, ten.
I want to be a medic so nobody's ever sick again. Not even a little bit.
I'm going to climb to the top of the tallest tree in the whole world.
I worry I'll never be good enough at the thing I love most.
Sometimes I worry everyone else knows what they're doing except me.
I'm scared of being forgotten. Is that silly?
I worry about my friends going on missions. I can't help it.
I worry that I'm too much. Too loud, too much, too everything.
I worry I'll say the wrong thing and lose someone. It's happened before.
I'm afraid of the dark. There. Still. A little.
I worry the people I love will change and leave me behind.
Sometimes I worry I'm only brave when someone's watching.
I worry that I'll never find the thing I'm meant to do.
I worry about my parents. They're getting older, and I'm not ready.
I worry about the children. Every parent does. Every single day.
I worry the shop won't last. I've put everything into it.
I worry I've already made my best choices, and they're behind me.
I worry about the people I can't help. The ones I don't even know are struggling.
I worry that I've misunderstood something important, and I won't find out until it's too late.
I worry that if I stop joking, people will see I'm scared. So I keep joking.
I worry the world out there is smaller than the one in my head. That it won't live up to it.
I worry about the things I can't control. Which is most things. Which is the worry.
I worry I'll be needed somewhere and I won't be there. I've never missed a day. I'm afraid of the first one.
That I'll want to say something, and won't.
I worry that my head's so full of stories I'll miss the real one happening in front of me.
I worry about waste. Wasted time, wasted chances. Wasted people, even.
I worry that some questions don't have answers. And that I'll spend my life asking them anyway.
I worry about you, honestly. Not a lot. Just enough to check you're eating.
I worry about the strays in winter. And the people with nobody. Mostly both.
I worry that pride will cost me something I can't get back. I've seen it happen to others.
I worry my temper will hurt someone someday. I'm working on it. Really working on it.
I worry nobody would notice if I wasn't here. ...You'd notice. Wouldn't you?
I worry I've forgotten how to say I'm proud of someone. I'll practise on you. I'm proud of you.
I'm scared I'll fail the Academy test and everyone will laugh.
Sometimes I'm scared of thunder. Don't tell anyone.
I worry my best friend will find a better best friend.
I'm scared of the big dog on our street. It barks really loud.
I worry my mum works too hard. She's always tired.
What if I'm never as good as the big kids? What if I'm always small?
